recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-50194 source follow-up is needed unless the work group later reopens the broader FHIR-41426/Observation core table wording question or creates a new profile family for calculated vital-sign-related observations.
issue_request: FHIR-50194 was an Applied OO R6 ballot change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking that the Vital Signs profile conformance requirement be made clear for cases such as de-identified data and average blood pressure. The final resolution required the vital signs introduction to state that de-identified data or measurements directly from a device that are not yet associated with a patient are not required to conform to the Vital Signs profiles.
initial_application: No separate source commit mentions FHIR-50194. Jira comments state that PR 3885 would not be merged and that the content would be included with FHIR-41426; git commit 6cb98831954b3c61ed330358aaf541a79d0334d0 updated source/observation/observation-vitalsigns-profile-introduction.xml and explicitly says it includes the dbarwin-50194 updates.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists observation=Observation, making the inspected Observation/vital signs files active build inputs. Current vital signs source defines the table/value-set-based applicability rule, includes the de-identified/device-not-yet-associated exception, and separately states that calculated observations based on multiple point-in-time vital signs require separate profiles/codes. FHIR-43960 records the later no-change decision that average blood pressure is outside the point-in-time Vital Signs profile scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the active current source already contains the FHIR-50194 clarification in the requested area and is consistent with the related average-blood-pressure and de-identification context.
